questions.q: What PySpark pattern does building a gold table primarily rely on?
options: Unity Catalog permission grants
groupBy()/.agg(), exactly as covered in Foundations Lessons 53-54, applied to silver's clean data
Only raw SQL, never the DataFrame API
A completely new aggregation API unique to Delta Lake
questions.explain: Nothing new here — gold just aims that same pattern at silver's clean, trustworthy data.

questions.q: Why are gold tables typically much smaller than the silver tables that fed them?
options: Gold tables randomly sample a subset of silver's rows
The expensive aggregation already happened once when gold was built, so a query against gold doesn't recompute it on every read
Gold tables cannot store more than 1000 rows by design
Gold tables only exist temporarily and are deleted after use
questions.explain: This size difference is the entire point — a dashboard querying gold directly is fast because of it.

questions.q: Is it a problem that gold.daily_revenue is a poor fit for answering a question about average trip distance by pickup zone?
options: Yes, every gold table should be able to answer any business question
No — that's the design. One gold table answers one specific question well; a different question gets its own gold table
This situation should never occur if silver was built correctly
Yes, this means the gold table was built incorrectly
questions.explain: Real medallion pipelines build multiple gold tables from the same silver data, each shaped for a specific need.

questions.q: Is building multiple gold tables from the same silver source normal or wasteful?
options: It violates medallion architecture's core design principle
Wasteful — silver should be queried directly instead of building multiple gold tables
It's only acceptable if the tables are combined back into one afterward
Normal — gold isn't one table, it's however many tables the business actually needs, each cheap to query for its specific purpose
questions.explain: Each gold table is shaped for a specific downstream need, with its aggregation already done.

questions.q: What does gold.daily_revenue in the example actually answer?
options: How many Unity Catalog users have access to the trips table
The average trip distance by pickup zone
Which rows in bronze were malformed
How much revenue per vendor, per day
questions.explain: This is exactly the specific business question that table's groupBy/agg was built to answer.
